summary:
We have designed our website as a museum for equipment left behind in space—whether because its mission had concluded or because it was intentionally left there to continue its work.
The experience begins when the user enters the site and finds themselves in space, with the Moon, Earth, and Mars in view. By clicking on one of these planets, the user can see specific locations where equipment—either sent there or abandoned—is situated. Selecting one of these locations reveals comprehensive details about the equipment, including its original mission, the date it was sent, its purpose, how its journey ended, and a collection of images.
details: The Space Museum is a unique scientific project. Upon entering the website, users are presented with three destinations: Earth, the Moon, and Mars. Selecting any of these reveals the locations of machines and robots that humans have left behind or sent there—what we refer to as “space artifacts.” Clicking on one of these machines opens a dedicated page featuring a photo gallery and comprehensive information about it. This platform is a valuable resource for students and researchers—as every piece of information, image, or other content is fully documented and sourced from reliable origins—and it is equally engaging for anyone with a passion for space.
